Comprehensive Guide to Laser Parameters for Laser Cutting
summary: Learn more about the various parameters when it come to laser cutting.
body_text: Laser-cutting machines are versatile machines that can make complex cuts and patterns using a powerful laser. They cut or engrave materials by vaporizing select portions of the workpiece. They are rapidly becoming more popular due to their non-contact nature and ability to consistently produce smooth and pristine cuts. Laser-cutting systems are useful in both industrial settings and craft and hobbyist environments. Certain properties, or laser parameters, such as power, wavelength, and polarization, characterize the behavior of the laser. You won’t achieve the highest-quality cutting results unless you first understand the parameters and the ways they impact the final product. This article will discuss the ideal laser parameters, their definitions, and their benefits. What Are the Parameters of a Laser? Users must familiarize themselves with seven laser parameters to properly optimize for their particular laser-cutting projects. These laser parameters are described below: 1. Power Power refers to the total energy that is emitted from a laser per second. Different laser-cutting systems have different maximum power ratings. Power is an important laser parameter because it defines how much energy goes into the operation, and potentially, how deep the cut will be. 2. Wavelength The wavelength, typically recorded in nanometers (nm), refers to the color of the light emitted from the laser. More specifically, it relates to the frequency and energy of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the laser. Shorter wavelengths (such as ultraviolet) have higher frequencies than longer ones (like infrared) and consequently, also have higher energy. The wavelengths used in laser systems range from infrared to ultraviolet, with visible light falling in between. 3. Polarization The polarization of a laser beam refers to the direction in which the beam’s emitted electric field resonates. It is controlled by the specific optical equipment in the laser system. Polarization is an important laser parameter because it characterizes how materials both reflect and absorb light. There are many different ways in which a laser beam can be polarized. However, circular and elliptical polarization are the two most commonly found in laser-cutting devices. Circular polarization means the orientation of the emitted electric field changes by 360° within a single wavelength. Elliptical polarization is similar in that its orientation changes by 360°. However, this change can occur over the span of multiple wavelengths. Polarization affects laser-cutting operations differently depending on the beam’s angle of incidence. This is the angle at which the laser contacts the workpiece material. Metal workpieces can demand incidence angles as high as 70 to 80°. A high incidence angle coupled with circular or elliptical polarization can improve laser absorption rates by as much as 80% compared to linearly polarized light. That means the workpiece absorbs more energy and takes less time to cut. Users sometimes need to modify their lasers so they put out circularly polarized light. 4. Cooling Cooling is an important laser parameter simply because the laser head generates heat while operating. Proper cooling keeps the laser optics at a more optimal temperature throughout its operation. This not only improves workpiece quality but also prolongs the laser system’s functional lifetime. 5. Pulse Width Pulse width refers to the length of time between the start and end of a single laser pulse (the short firing of a laser). It is an important laser parameter because it characterizes how much energy is allowed to accumulate in the laser over a given period. This can affect laser cut quality and cutting speed. 6. Coherence Length Coherence length refers to the distance the laser can travel before its light falls out of phase and becomes scattered. 7. Spot Size Spot size is the total diameter of the laser beam as determined by the focal length of its focusing lens. Smaller spot sizes concentrate more energy in a smaller area, while larger spot sizes deliver less energy per unit area. What Are Laser Parameters? Laser parameters refer to the different properties that characterize the behavior of a particular laser. It’s important to understand these parameters and how they impact the laser’s performance and cut quality. Once you master these ideas, you’ll be able to choose the best settings for any project, workpiece, or material you choose. What Are the Benefits of Understanding Laser Parameters? Your thorough understanding of laser parameters will aid you throughout the laser-cutting process. The knowledge is critical to properly configuring your laser system to cut or engrave specific materials. Plus, you can develop more efficient processes overall.

Top Dermatologist-Recommended Supplements for Beautiful Skin
summary: Discover best supplements for glowing skin including Vitamins C and E, omega-3 fatty acids, and probiotics and how to incorporate these nutrients into your diet!
body_text: Without a doubt, we all want to have beautiful, glowing, and healthy skin. While there are numerous external products and treatments that can assist us in achieving this look, what we put into our bodies is equally important. In this post, we'll look at some of the best supplements for glowing skin. Vitamins C and E, omega-3 fatty acids, and probiotics are examples. You can help your skin look its best from the inside out by incorporating these nutrients into your diet! Vitamin D : This vitamin is essential for overall skin health and can help reduce inflammation and prevent premature aging . Omega-3 Fatty Acids : Found in fish oil, these fatty acids help nourish the skin from the inside out, reducing inflammation and promoting a healthy complexion. Probiotics : Probiotics help to balance the gut microbiome, which in turn can improve the appearance of skin by reducing inflammation and promoting a healthy immune system. Collagen : Collagen supplements may help improve skin elasticity, reduce wrinkles and fine lines, and promote healthy hair and nails. Vitamin C : This vitamin is essential for collagen production and can help protect the skin from sun damage and other environmental stressors. It's important to note that supplements should be taken under the guidance of a healthcare provider and that they should not be used as a replacement for a healthy diet and lifestyle. Additionally, the effectiveness of supplements may vary from person to person, and results may take time to show. How to choose the right supplements for skin When choosing supplements for skin health, it is important to consider several factors such as your specific skin concerns, lifestyle, and medical history. Here are some tips to help you choose the right supplements for your skin: Identify your skin concerns : Take a closer look at your skin and determine what issues you want to address. Do you have dry or oily skin? Are you dealing with acne , fine lines, or wrinkles? Do you have dark spots or hyperpigmentation ? Once you identify your specific skin concerns, you can narrow down your supplement options. Consult a healthcare professional : Before adding any supplements to your routine, it is always best to consult a healthcare professional such as a dermatologist, nutritionist, or doctor. They can recommend supplements that are safe and effective for your specific needs and can also advise you on the appropriate dosage. Look for key ingredients : When choosing supplements for skin health, look for key ingredients that have been shown to improve skin appearance and function. Examples include vitamin C, vitamin E , vitamin A, collagen, biotin , and omega-3 fatty acids . However, it is important to note that not all supplements containing these ingredients are created equal, so make sure to choose high-quality supplements from reputable brands. Consider your lifestyle : Your lifestyle can also play a role in your skin health. For example, if you spend a lot of time in the sun, you may want to consider a supplement with antioxidants to protect your skin from UV damage. If you have a poor diet, a multivitamin or a supplement that contains key nutrients may be beneficial. Be patient : It is important to remember that supplements take time to work. It can take several weeks or even months to see improvements in your skin, so be patient and consistent with your supplement routine. Overall, choosing the right supplements for your skin requires careful consideration and consultation with a healthcare professional. By identifying your specific skin concerns, looking for key ingredients, and considering your lifestyle, you can choose supplements that can help improve the appearance and health of your skin. Antioxidants for comprehensive skin repair Antioxidants are essential for comprehensive skin repair because they neutralise free radicals, reduce oxidative stress, and protect the skin from environmental and UV damage. Here are some important antioxidants that are beneficial to skin health and repair: Vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that brightens the skin, reduces hyperpigmentation, and increases collagen production. It also protects the skin against UV rays, neutralises free radicals, and promotes wound healing. For best results, incorporate vitamin C serums or creams into your skincare routine. Vitamin E is another powerful antioxidant that protects the skin from oxidative stress and UV-induced damage. It moisturises the skin, fortifies the skin barrier, and promotes healing. Look for vitamin E-containing skincare products or include vitamin E-rich foods like almonds, sunflower seeds, and spinach in your diet. Green tea extract is high in polyphenols , specifically epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), which has powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Green tea extract protects the skin from UV rays, reduces inflammation, and improves tone and texture. Look for skincare products that contain green tea extract, or drink green tea regularly to benefit your skin. Resveratrol is a potent antioxidant found in grapes, red wine, and berries. It protects the skin from oxidative stress, reduces inflammation, and increases collagen production. Resveratrol can be found in skincare products or taken as a supplement to improve skin health. The body naturally produces coenzyme Q10, an antioxidant that helps neutralise free radicals and protect cells from oxidative damage. It also improves cellular energy production and collagen synthesis. Look for CoQ10-containing skincare products to help reduce wrinkles and improve skin firmness. Astaxanthin is a carotenoid antioxidant found in some seafood, algae, and red fruits such as tomatoes and watermelon. It protects the skin from UV rays, reduces inflammation, and improves elasticity and hydration. Consider taking astaxanthin supplements or using astaxanthin-containing skincare products to improve your skin. Niacinamide is a versatile antioxidant that enhances skin texture, reduces hyperpigmentation, and strengthens the skin barrier. It also has anti-inflammatory properties and helps to regulate oil production. Incorporate niacinamide serums or creams into your skincare routine to promote overall skin repair. Selenium is a trace mineral with antioxidant properties that protects the skin from oxidative stress and UV rays. It also stimulates DNA repair and collagen synthesis, resulting in better skin health and appearance. Include selenium-rich foods in your diet, such as Brazil nuts, seafood, and whole grains, for skin benefits. By incorporating these antioxidant-rich ingredients into your skincare routine and diet, you can promote overall skin repair, reduce ageing signs, and keep your complexion looking healthy and radiant. Zinc and Selenium's role in skin health Zinc and selenium are essential minerals that promote skin health and overall well-being. Here's how each of these minerals improves skin health: 1. Zinc : Zinc is essential for wound healing and tissue repair. It promotes cell growth, collagen synthesis, and immune function, all of which are necessary for keeping skin healthy and facilitating healing. Zinc's anti-inflammatory properties can help reduce inflammation and redness caused by acne, eczema, and other skin conditions. It may also help regulate oil production and alleviate acne symptoms. Zinc is an antioxidant, which helps to protect the skin from free radicals and environmental stressors. It helps to reduce oxidative stress, which can lead to premature ageing and skin damage. Zinc is essential for skin health because it supports the immune system. It protects against infections and strengthens the body's natural defence mechanisms. 2. Selenium : Selenium is an effective antioxidant that protects the skin from oxidative damage caused by free radicals, UV radiation, and environmental pollutants. It helps to neutralise harmful molecules and reduce oxidative stress, which can lead to premature ageing and skin damage. Selenium has been linked to a lower risk of skin cancer, particularly non-melanoma types such as basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. It protects against DNA damage and promotes repair mechanisms in skin cells. Selenium aids in wound healing and tissue repair by promoting cell growth, collagen synthesis, and immune response. Adequate selenium levels are necessary for optimal wound healing and skin regeneration. Selenium is important for immune function and helps support the body's natural defense mechanisms against infections and pathogens. A healthy immune system is essential for maintaining overall skin health and preventing skin infections. Evaluating supplements: Safety and efficacy When evaluating supplements for safety and efficacy, several factors should be considered to ensure that you are selecting high-quality products that are both safe and beneficial to your health. Here are some important considerations: Ingredients : Check the ingredient list to ensure that the supplement contains the active ingredients in the proper doses. Look for standardised supplements to ensure consistency and efficacy. Avoid supplements with unnecessary fillers, artificial colours, flavours, or preservatives. Quality and Purity : Select supplements from reputable brands that follow good manufacturing practices (GMP) and have been independently tested for quality and purity. Look for third-party certifications from organisations that guarantee the quality and purity of supplements, such as NSF International, USP (United States Pharmacopoeia), or ConsumerLab.com. Bioavailability : Take into account the supplement's active ingredients' bioavailability, which is the degree to which the body can absorb and use them. Choose supplements that contain bioavailable forms of nutrients for maximum efficacy. Research and Evidence : Look for scientific research and clinical studies that support the supplement's safety and efficacy for the intended use. If you want information based on evidence, check reliable sources like academic institutions, government health agencies, or peer-reviewed journals. Dosage and Safety : To ensure safety and efficacy, follow the manufacturer's or healthcare professional's recommended dosage guidelines. Avoid exceeding the recommended dosage, as this can increase the risk of side effects or toxicity. Before beginning any new supplement regimen, speak with a healthcare professional, especially if you have underlying health conditions or are taking medications. Potential Interactions : Be aware of any potential interactions between supplements, medications, or other supplements you may be using. Some supplements may interact with medications or other supplements, resulting in adverse effects or reduced efficacy. Consult a healthcare professional or chemist for advice on possible interactions. Manufacturer Reputation : Select supplements from reputable manufacturers with a track record of producing high-quality goods. To ensure that you are purchasing supplements from a reliable source, look into the manufacturer's reputation, history, and commitment to quality. Customer Reviews and Feedback : Read customer reviews and feedback to learn more about how other people have used the supplement. However, keep in mind that individual reactions to supplements can differ, and what works for one person may not work for another. Cost and Value : Evaluate the supplement's cost and value about its quality, efficacy, and intended use. While price can be an indicator of quality, it is critical to prioritise value and select supplements that provide the best balance of quality and efficacy within your budget. By carefully evaluating supplements for safety and efficacy using these criteria, you can make informed choices and select high-quality products that promote your health and well-being. Always consult with a healthcare professional before beginning a new supplement regimen, especially if you have any underlying health conditions or concerns. How to incorporate supplements into your routine Incorporating supplements into your daily routine can help you maintain a healthy lifestyle, but you should do so safely and effectively. Here are some steps you can take to incorporate supplements into your daily routine: Before beginning any new supplement regimen, consult with a healthcare professional. They can advise you on which supplements are safe and effective for you based on your specific health requirements, medications, and medical background. Conduct your research on the supplements you are considering taking. To ensure that the supplement is safe and effective, consult reputable sources such as scientific studies or government agencies. Look for supplements from reputable companies that use high-quality ingredients and adhere to good manufacturing practices. Avoid supplements that are poorly manufactured or make unrealistic claims. Always follow the recommended dosage on the supplement label or as prescribed by your healthcare professional. Taking too much of a supplement can be harmful. Incorporate supplements into your routine: Once you have decided on your supplements and calculated the recommended dosage, work them into your daily routine. Set a reminder to take your supplements at the same time every day so you do not forget. Keep track of how you feel after using the supplements. If you experience any side effects, stop taking the supplement and consult with your doctor. Timing and dosage for optimal benefits The timing and dose of supplements have a considerable impact on their effectiveness and safety. Some general guidelines for optimising supplement timing and dosage for maximum benefits include following recommended dosage, consistency is key, timing with meals, dividing dosage throughout the day, individual needs and goals, timing for specific nutrients, being mindful of interactions, and listening to your body. By following these scheduling and dosage guidelines, you may improve the effectiveness and safety of your supplements while also supporting your general health and well-being. Always consult with a healthcare expert before beginning a new supplement regimen, especially if you have any underlying health conditions or concerns. Combining supplements with topical treatments Combining vitamins and topical treatments can be an effective way to address specific skin conditions while also providing overall skincare benefits. Understanding your skin concerns, consulting with a healthcare professional, considering synergistic ingredients, optimising absorption and efficacy, being mindful of interactions, starting slowly and monitoring effects, maintaining consistency, and following product instructions are all factors to consider when combining supplements with topical treatments. By intelligently mixing vitamins and topical treatments under the supervision of a healthcare professional, you can more effectively address your skincare concerns and attain healthier, more vibrant skin. Lifestyle factors affecting supplement absorption Several lifestyle factors can influence supplement absorption, thereby affecting efficacy and overall benefits. Here are some important lifestyle factors to consider. Dietary Habits : The way you eat affects how well you absorb supplements. Certain nutrients may be better absorbed with food, while others are best absorbed on an empty stomach. For example, fat-soluble vitamins such as vitamin D, vitamin E, and vitamin K are better absorbed when consumed with a fat-rich meal. On the other hand, some minerals, such as iron and calcium, may compete for absorption with certain foods or beverages, with calcium inhibiting iron absorption when consumed together. Consider timing your supplements with your meals to maximise absorption. Hydration Status : Adequate hydration is required for optimal nutrient absorption. Water aids in the dissolution and transportation of nutrients throughout the body, allowing for better absorption in the digestive tract. Dehydration can impair nutrient absorption, reducing the efficacy of supplements. Ensure you drink enough water throughout the day, especially when taking supplements, to support optimal absorption. Digestive Health : The health of your digestive system might have an impact on how well you absorb nutrients from supplements. Digestive problems, such as gastrointestinal illnesses, food allergies, inflammation, or malabsorption, can impair nutrient absorption and diminish the effectiveness of supplements. Addressing underlying digestive disorders with a healthy diet, lifestyle changes, and focused therapies can improve nutrient absorption and supplement efficacy. Medication Use : Certain drugs can impair the absorption, metabolism, or utilisation of nutrients from supplements. Antacids, proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), and some antibiotics can all suppress stomach acid production, which is required for mineral absorption such as calcium, magnesium, and iron. Other drugs may disrupt certain nutritional pathways or compete for absorption. Consult a healthcare expert or chemist to determine how your drugs may affect supplement absorption and whether adjustments are required. Alcohol and Caffeine Consumption : Excessive alcohol consumption can reduce nutritional absorption and deplete the body's critical vitamins and minerals. Similarly, excessive coffee intake may impair the absorption of some nutrients, such as calcium, magnesium, and iron. Limiting alcohol and caffeine consumption and scheduling supplements away from periods of high alcohol or caffeine use may help optimise absorption. Stress and Lifestyle Factors : Chronic stress, lack of sleep, smoking, and other lifestyle choices can all influence gut function and nutritional absorption. Stress can disrupt gastrointestinal motility, diminish stomach acid production, and change the composition of the gut flora, all of which can have an impact on nutritional absorption. Prioritising stress management techniques, getting enough sleep, and living a healthy lifestyle may help with nutrient absorption and supplement effectiveness. Individual Variability : Individual variances in genetics, age, metabolism, and overall health state can all affect supplement absorption. Genetic variations in nutrient metabolic pathways, age-related changes in digestive function, and underlying health issues can all affect how well your body absorbs and uses nutrients from supplements. Tailoring your supplement regimen to your specific needs, as well as seeking personalised advice from a healthcare professional, can help you maximise absorption and efficacy. Go to supplements for skin health There are several supplements that can help improve skin health. Here are some of the most commonly recommended ones: Vitamin C : This antioxidant helps protect skin cells from damage caused by free radicals and can also help boost collagen production, which can help keep skin firm and smooth. Vitamin E : Another powerful antioxidant, vitamin E can help protect skin from sun damage and may also help reduce the appearance of scars. Omega-3 fatty acids : Found in fish oil and other supplements, omega-3s can help reduce inflammation in the body, which may improve skin health and reduce the risk of acne and other skin conditions. Zinc : Zinc is essential for healthy skin, as it helps regulate oil production and can also help reduce inflammation. Probiotics : These "friendly" bacteria can help improve gut health, which may in turn improve skin health by reducing inflammation and promoting healthy digestion. Collagen : Collagen supplements are said to help improve skin elasticity and reduce wrinkles, as collagen is a protein that makes up a significant portion of our skin. It's important to note that supplements should never be a replacement for a healthy diet and lifestyle. Always speak with your healthcare provider before starting any new supplement regimen, as some supplements may interact with certain medications or health conditions. Collagen and Hyaluronic acid for hydration and elasticity Collagen and hyaluronic acid are two essential skin components that help maintain hydration, elasticity, and overall skin health. 1. Collagen : Collagen is a protein that helps the skin retain hydration while also providing structural support. It forms a network of fibres that retain water molecules, keeping the skin hydrated and plump. Collagen fibres provide the skin with strength and elasticity, allowing it to stretch and return to its original shape. As we age, collagen production declines, leading to a loss of elasticity and the formation of wrinkles and fine lines. Collagen is vital for wound healing and tissue repair. It promotes the growth of new skin cells and aids in the skin's natural regeneration process. Collagen supplements come in a variety of forms, including powders, capsules, and liquid formulations. They contain hydrolyzed collagen peptides, which are broken down into smaller molecules to facilitate absorption. Taking collagen supplements may help to improve skin hydration, elasticity, and overall appearance, especially as we age and collagen production naturally declines. 2. Hyaluronic Acid : Hyaluronic acid is a molecule that can hold up to 1000 times its weight in water, making it extremely effective for hydrating the skin. It draws moisture into the skin, keeping it hydrated, smooth, and supple. Hyaluronic acid promotes skin elasticity by plumping it and filling in fine lines and wrinkles. It also helps to maintain the structure of the skin's extracellular matrix, giving it a firmer, more youthful appearance. Hyaluronic acid aids wound healing by promoting the formation of new blood vessels and facilitating the migration of skin cells to the site of injury. It contributes to an optimal environment for tissue repair and regeneration. Hyaluronic acid is widely used in skincare products like serums, moisturisers , and masks due to its hydrating and plumping properties. When applied topically, hyaluronic acid penetrates the skin and provides both immediate and long-term hydration. Vitamin C, E, and Omega-3 fatty acids for antioxidant support Vitamin C, vitamin E, and omega-3 fatty acids are potent antioxidants that help maintain overall health and protect the body from oxidative stress and inflammation. Here's how each of these nutrients helps with antioxidant support: 1. Vitamin C : Vitamin C is a powerful water-soluble antioxidant that aids in the elimination of free radicals and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the body. Free radicals are unstable molecules that cause oxidative damage to cells, proteins, and DNA, resulting in ageing, inflammation, and chronic diseases. Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis, which is critical for maintaining skin elasticity, wound healing, and overall skin health. Collagen is a protein that gives structural support to the skin, bones, and connective tissues. Vitamin C improves immune function by increasing the production and function of white blood cells, which are responsible for fighting infections and pathogens. It also helps to shorten the duration and severity of common colds and respiratory infections. Vitamin C has photoprotective properties, which can help protect the skin from UV-induced damage caused by sun exposure. It scavenges free radicals produced by UV radiation and aids in DNA repair in skin cells. 2. Vitamin E : Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes, lipids, and lipoproteins against oxidative damage. It works together with vitamin C to neutralise free radicals and prevent lipid peroxidation, which can cause cellular damage and inflammation. Vitamin E promotes skin health and integrity by protecting it from oxidative stress, UV radiation, and environmental pollutants. It promotes skin barrier function, hydration, and elasticity, thereby preventing premature ageing and wrinkles. Vitamin E has been shown to protect the heart by reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and arterial plaque formation. It may improve blood vessel function, lower blood pressure, and decrease the risk of cardiovascular disease. Vitamin E promotes immune function by increasing immune cell activity and modulating immune responses. It helps protect immune cells from oxidative damage and supports their ability to mount an effective immune response against infections. 3. Omega-3 Fatty Acids : Omega-3 fatty acids, particularly eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), have potent anti-inflammatory properties that help reduce inflammation and oxidative stress in the body. Chronic inflammation is a risk factor for many chronic diseases, including heart disease, arthritis, and cancer. Omega-3 fatty acids promote heart health by lowering triglycerides, lowering blood pressure, improving blood vessel function, and reducing inflammation. They help prevent blood clots and plaque buildup in the arteries, which lowers the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Omega-3 fatty acids are required for optimal brain health and cognitive function. They are important components of the brain's cell membranes, supporting neurotransmitter function, synaptic plasticity, and neuron communication. Omega-3s have been linked to better mood, memory, and cognitive performance. Omega-3 fatty acids promote skin health and hydration by strengthening the lipid barrier and lowering inflammation. They can help alleviate the symptoms of inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, and acne while also promoting a healthy, radiant complexion. Probiotics for gut health and skin clarity Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that promote a healthy balance of microorganisms in the digestive tract. Through their effects on the gut-skin axis, probiotics may also support skin health and clarity, according to emerging research. Probiotics have the following potential benefits for gut health and skin clarity: Gut Health : Probiotics help to restore and maintain a healthy balance of beneficial bacteria in the gut, which is required for proper digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function. They compete with harmful bacteria for nutrients and space, preventing the overgrowth of pathogenic microorganisms that can harm gut health. Probiotics can help relieve digestive symptoms like bloating, gas, constipation, and diarrhoea by encouraging regular bowel movements, reducing inflammation, and restoring gut barrier function. They may also help with the symptoms of IBS, IBD, and other gastrointestinal disorders. The gut contains a significant portion of the body's immune system, and probiotics play an important role in regulating immune responses and protecting against infections. Probiotics increase the production of immunoglobulins, cytokines, and other immune factors, thereby strengthening the body's natural defence mechanisms. Skin Clarity : Imbalances in gut microbiota and dysregulation of the immune system can contribute to systemic inflammation, which is associated with skin conditions such as acne, eczema, and rosacea. Probiotics help modulate immune responses and reduce inflammation, which may help alleviate symptoms of inflammatory skin conditions and promote clearer skin. The gut-skin axis refers to the bidirectional communication between the gut and the skin, where imbalances in gut microbiota can affect skin health and vice versa. Probiotics support gut barrier function, which may indirectly influence skin barrier function by reducing intestinal permeability and systemic inflammation. A healthy gut barrier helps prevent the translocation of harmful toxins and pathogens from the gut into the bloodstream, which can contribute to skin inflammation and breakouts. Probiotics may also directly influence the composition and diversity of the skin microbiota, which plays a role in maintaining skin health and preventing colonization by pathogenic bacteria. By promoting a healthy balance of skin microorganisms, probiotics may help reduce the risk of skin infections and improve skin clarity. Green tea extract and Turmeric for anti-inflammatory benefits Green tea extract and turmeric are two natural ingredients known for their powerful anti-inflammatory properties, which can provide a variety of health benefits, including improved skin health. Here's how each of these ingredients works and how they can be useful: Green Tea Extract : Green tea extract contains polyphenols, particularly catechins, which have powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. These antioxidants help to neutralise free radicals, reduce oxidative stress, and protect cells from UV radiation, pollution, and other environmental stressors. Green tea extract contains catechins, which have been shown to inhibit the activity of inflammatory enzymes and cytokines, thereby reducing inflammation and soothing irritated skin. Frequent ingestion of green tea or topical application of green tea extract can help reduce redness and inflammation linked to inflammatory skin conditions such as rosacea, eczema, and acne. Green tea extract possesses photoprotective qualities that could aid in shielding the skin from UV-induced deterioration. It helps prevent sunburn, early ageing, and skin cancer by scavenging free radicals produced by UV radiation, reducing inflammation, and promoting DNA repair in skin cells. Turmeric : Turmeric's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant qualities are attributed to a bioactive substance called curcumin. The therapeutic effects of curcumin on a range of medical conditions, including inflammatory skin disorders, have been thoroughly investigated. Curcumin inhibits the actions of cytokines and inflammatory enzymes that are important in the inflammatory process, such as tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). By modulating these pathways, curcumin helps reduce inflammation and alleviate symptoms of inflammatory skin conditions like psoriasis, eczema, and acne. Turmeric also has antimicrobial properties, which can help fight acne-causing bacteria and other pathogens that cause skin infections and inflammation. Applying turmeric topically or consuming it orally may help promote clearer, healthier skin by targeting the underlying causes of acne and other inflammatory skin conditions. In addition to anti-inflammatory properties, curcumin has been shown to inhibit melanin production and reduce hyperpigmentation, resulting in a brighter, more even skin tone. Incorporating turmeric-based skincare products or consuming turmeric supplements may help improve skin clarity and reduce the appearance of dark spots and blemishes. Niacinamide and Coenzyme Q10 for skin barrier and rejuvenation Niacinamide (vitamin B3) and coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) are two powerful skincare ingredients known for their ability to strengthen and rejuvenate the skin barrier. Here's how each of these ingredients works and what they do for skin health: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3) : Niacinamide strengthens the skin barrier by increasing the production of ceramides, fatty acids, and cholesterol, all of which are necessary components of the lipid barrier. A strong skin barrier retains moisture, protects against environmental aggressors, and prevents trans-epidermal water loss (TEWL), resulting in hydrated, healthier-looking skin. Niacinamide has anti-inflammatory properties that help to reduce redness, soothe irritation, and relieve symptoms of inflammatory skin conditions such as acne, rosacea, and eczema. It reduces the release of pro-inflammatory mediators and regulates inflammatory pathways, making it ideal for sensitive and reactive skin. Evens Skin Tone: Niacinamide regulates melanin production, which reduces hyperpigmentation, dark spots, and uneven skin tone. It inhibits melanin transfer to the skin's surface and promotes more even pigment distribution, resulting in a brighter, more radiant complexion. Niacinamide regulates sebum production and reduces pore size, making it ideal for oily and acne-prone skin. By balancing oil production and preventing pore congestion, niacinamide helps minimize the appearance of enlarged pores and promote smoother, clearer skin. Niacinamide is an antioxidant that helps neutralise free radicals and protects the skin from oxidative damage caused by UV radiation, pollution, and other environmental stressors. It helps prevent premature aging, fine lines, and wrinkles, resulting in a more youthful-looking complexion. Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) : Coenzyme Q10 is a powerful antioxidant that helps neutralize free radicals and protect the skin from oxidative stress. It helps prevent collagen degradation, DNA damage, and lipid peroxidation, preserving the skin's youthfulness and resilience. CoQ10 plays a key role in cellular energy production, providing the energy needed for cell metabolism, repair, and regeneration. As we age, CoQ10 levels in the skin decline, leading to reduced energy production and slower cellular turnover. Supplementing with CoQ10 can help replenish cellular energy stores and support skin rejuvenation. CoQ10 stimulates collagen production and promotes the synthesis of elastin fibers, which are essential for maintaining skin elasticity and firmness. By boosting collagen synthesis, CoQ10 helps reduce the appearance of fine lines, wrinkles, and sagging skin, resulting in a smoother, more youthful complexion. CoQ10 has been shown to speed up wound healing and tissue repair by stimulating angiogenesis (the formation of new blood vessels) and increasing fibroblast activity. It improves skin barrier function, reduces inflammation, and promotes the skin's natural regeneration process, resulting in faster healing and less scarring. CoQ10 has photoprotective properties, which can help protect the skin from UV-induced damage caused by sun exposure. It scavenges free radicals produced by UV radiation, reduces oxidative stress, and strengthens the skin's natural defence mechanisms, thereby preventing sunburn, photoaging, and skin cancer. Resveratrol and Curcumin for anti-aging and healing Resveratrol and curcumin are two potent natural compounds with anti-aging and healing properties that have recently received a lot of attention in skincare and health research. Here's how each of these ingredients works and what they mean for anti-aging and healing: Resveratrol : Resveratrol, a polyphenol found in grapes, red wine, berries, and some plants, has antioxidant properties. It is well-known for its strong antioxidant properties, which help neutralise free radicals and protect cells from oxidative damage caused by environmental stressors like UV radiation, pollution, and inflammation. Resveratrol has anti-inflammatory properties, which help to reduce inflammation and soothe irritated skin. By inhibiting inflammatory pathways and modulating immune responses, resveratrol helps calm redness, minimize swelling, and alleviate symptoms of inflammatory skin conditions like acne, eczema, and rosacea. Resveratrol stimulates collagen production and promotes the synthesis of elastin fibres, which are required for skin elasticity and firmness. title: Dr ChatGPT, tell me what I want to hear: How prompt knowledge impacts health answer correctness
summary: Tutorials, guides and deep dives into the best techniques and research for building reliable AI.
body_text: Do not index Original Paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13793 Blog URL blog.athina.ai /dr-chat...rectness Original Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13793 By: Guido Zuccon , Bevan Koopman Abstract: Generative pre-trained language models (GPLMs) like ChatGPT encode in the model's parameters knowledge the models observe during the pre-training phase. This knowledge is then used at inference to address the task specified by the user in their prompt. For example, for the question-answering task, the GPLMs leverage the knowledge and linguistic patterns learned at training to produce an answer to a user question. Aside from the knowledge encoded in the model itself, answers produced by GPLMs can also leverage knowledge provided in the prompts. For example, a GPLM can be integrated into a retrieve-then-generate paradigm where a search engine is used to retrieve documents relevant to the question; the content of the documents is then transferred to the GPLM via the prompt. In this paper we study the differences in answer correctness generated by ChatGPT when leveraging the model's knowledge alone vs. in combination with the prompt knowledge. We study this in the context of consumers seeking health advice from the model. Aside from measuring the effectiveness of ChatGPT in this context, we show that the knowledge passed in the prompt can overturn the knowledge encoded in the model and this is, in our experiments, to the detriment of answer correctness. This work has important implications for the development of more robust and transparent question-answering systems based on generative pre-trained language models. Summary Notes The Impact of Prompt Knowledge on ChatGPT's Health Advice Accuracy Generative Pre-trained Language Models (GPLMs) like ChatGPT have significantly changed our interaction with technology, especially in healthcare. These AI models are adept at producing human-like text, making them useful for automating tasks, including providing health advice. Yet, their effectiveness in delivering accurate health advice greatly depends on the prompts users provide. This article explores the crucial role of prompt knowledge in the accuracy of health advice from ChatGPT, drawing on a study by Guido Zuccon and Bevan Koopman. Understanding Prompt Knowledge and GPLM Accuracy The study by Zuccon and Koopman highlights a critical element of AI interaction: the effect of prompt knowledge on the accuracy of responses from GPLMs. In healthcare advice, where precision is crucial, the study emphasizes the risks of inaccurate or misleading prompts. It points out the need for strong and clear QA systems capable of handling complex prompts to deliver dependable health advice. Study Methodology The research assessed ChatGPT's performance in giving health advice using the TREC Misinformation track through two different approaches: Question-only: ChatGPT provided answers based on its pre-trained knowledge without additional information. Evidence-biased: The model's responses were influenced by supplemental documents supporting or contradicting the health treatment in question. The study aimed to uncover: ChatGPT's effectiveness in answering complex health questions without extra information. The effect of supporting or contradicting evidence on the accuracy of ChatGPT's responses. Key Findings The study revealed: ChatGPT had an 80% accuracy in the question-only setup, showcasing its capability as a dependable source for health information. Introduction of evidence reduced accuracy to 63%. Misleading or incorrect evidence could lead ChatGPT to offer wrong advice, despite its ability to give correct answers without such biases. These findings highlight the importance of precise prompt engineering in affecting the accuracy of GPLM outputs in health advice. Recommendations for AI Engineers The insights from this study offer AI engineers guidelines to improve GPLM accuracy in health advice: Careful Prompt Design: Create clear, accurate prompts without misleading information, especially vital in healthcare. Robust Testing: Thoroughly test GPLM outputs with a variety of prompts to identify and correct potential biases or misinformation. Transparency and User Education: Inform users about GPLM limitations and guide them on effectively framing queries. Ongoing Monitoring: Continuously check GPLM performance in real-world applications to quickly address any issues. Conclusion Zuccon and Koopman's study provides a critical look at how prompt knowledge affects ChatGPT's health advice accuracy. It underscores the significance of prompt design in ensuring reliable GPLM outputs, particularly where inaccurate information can have serious repercussions. Moving forward, it's vital for AI engineers to integrate these findings into GPLM development and deployment, leading to more accurate and safe AI-driven health advice systems. References This article is based on the study "Dr ChatGPT, tell me what I want to hear: How prompt knowledge impacts health answer correctness" by Guido Zuccon and Bevan Koopman, among other sources on GPLMs' capabilities and challenges in healthcare. title: Rate limiting in Sails
summary: Rate limiting helps you control the rate of incoming requests to an API. In this article we go over how to set up rate limiting in Sails
body_text: I recently had to implement rate limiting on the Conference API - a Sailscasts community project. The whole idea of rate limiting is to limit the number of requests coming to a particular API in a certain time window. The Conference API is written with Sails.js and when researching on how to implement rate limiting, I stumbled on the express-rate-limit package which handles rate limiting for Express and since Sails is based on Express, I saw an opportunity to wrap this package in a Sails hook to fine-tune the experience of using the package for Sails developers. sails-hook-rate-limit The result of that fine-tuning is sails-hook-rate-limit . This hook simplifies setting up rate limiting in a Sails application by wrapping the express-rate-limit package thereby providing a nicer DX for setting up rate limiting in Sails. Installation To use this hook in your Sails project, run the below command in your terminal npm i sails-hook-rate-limit --save And that’s all you need to setup rate limiting in your Sails API! Setup By default, sails-hook-rate-limit set some basic configs that you may or may not want to override. For example, it sets the windowMs to 10 minutes , the max request per window to 100 , set express-rate-limit to use standard headers i.e RateLimit-* and disables legacy headers i.e X-RateLimit-* To override these values and more config options, create config/rate-limit.js and export a rateLimit object like so: module . exports .rateLimit = { // config goes here } In this config object you can pass in any configuration property that express-rate-limit expects. See the configuration docs of express-rate-limit for those properties. For example let’s say I want to override the default 10 minutes window to 20 minutes , I will pass the following to config/rate-limit.js object. module . exports .rateLimit = { windowMs: 20 * 60 * 1000 // 20 minutes } Conclusion Rate limiting is frequently used to control the frequency of requests to an API and in this article we covered how to set up rate limiting in your Sails APIs by using the sails-hook-rate-limit Sails hook.

body_text: Ao abrir um negócio, muitos empreendedores perdem o entusiasmo quando se trata de adquirir produtos para vendê-los, uma vez que não sabem a procedência e a qualidade do material. Neste aspecto, é importante saber onde e como encontrar fornecedores para bens de consumo . Logo, para o processo de comercialização, é necessário contar com parceiros competentes e confiáveis, que entregam bons materiais e dentro do prazo, com preços vantajosos. Mas, afinal, onde encontrar fornecedores para bens de consumo que atendam a essas expectativas? Se você está em dúvida, daremos dicas infalíveis para facilitar sua procura. Mas, antes disso, que tal conhecer mais sobre o “boom” do segmento? Continue com a gente e boa leitura! Crescimento do setor de bens de consumo Quando falamos em fornecedores de bens de consumo, nos referimos àqueles que disponibilizam produtos e estoques para outras lojas, principalmente. E não é à toa que os bens de consumo são uma área em expansão. Segundo a Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC), a Intenção de Consumo das Famílias (ICF) apresentou um crescimento em todos os meses de 2022, alcançando 80,2 pontos em junho , além de acumular um avanço de 10,1% no primeiro semestre do ano. Seguindo a tendência de sucesso do setor, é importante contar com bons fornecedores para tornar sua empresa uma potência no ramo dos negócios. Neste caso, você precisa ficar atento a uma série de critérios, sobre os quais falaremos adiante. Confira! Fornecedores nacionais ou internacionais: quais escolher? Para fazer uma escolha assertiva no fornecedor de bens de consumo, planeje se irá optar por parceiros nacionais ou do exterior. Isso dependerá do segmento em que sua empresa trabalha. Por exemplo, se for eletroeletrônicos, será que é mais rentável e seguro trazer produtos de fora do país? Nesse sentido, tanto os fornecedores nacionais quanto os internacionais têm suas vantagens e desvantagens. Vamos a elas: Fornecedores nacionais Vantagens: tempo de entrega mais ágil; maior qualidade de fabricação; maior segurança de pagamento; comunicação facilitada pela proximidade. Desvantagens menor opção de escolha de produtos, sendo que muitos não são fabricados no Brasil. Fornecedores internacionais Vantagens mais opções de fornecedores; serviços rápidos de entrega. Desvantagens baixa proteção de propriedade intelectual; dificuldade de administração em razão de barreiras como idioma, comunicação e fuso horário; menor segurança de pagamento. Bem, agora que você já tem um panorama do que considerar na hora de decidir por um fornecedor ou outro, venha conferir algumas formas de encontrar futuros parceiros. Como encontrar fornecedores para bens de consumo? 4 dicas A seguir, elencamos 4 opções para quem busca encontrar fornecedores de bens de consumo. 1. Pesquise na internet por palavras-chave Nos últimos anos, ficou muito fácil pesquisar por fornecedores na internet. No Google, por exemplo, você pode achar algumas opções nas páginas de resultados. Aqui, a indicação é usar termos de pesquisa variados, como: “fornecedores para eletrodomésticos”, “fornecedores internacionais de celulares” e afins. Essa filtragem irá aprimorar a qualidade das suas buscas e, consequentemente, dos resultados. 2. Geralmente, encontram-se depoimentos de clientes nos sites das empresas. Também é possível obter opiniões imparciais por meio de sites como Reclame Aqui e o Consumidor.gov.br . title: Scaling Accessibility Through Your Design System Panel Recap
summary: Find out the main takeaways from our fireside chat on scaling a11y through design systems. Get valuable insights from some of the industry's biggest experts.
body_text: We invited a panel of experts to discuss scaling a11y through your design system. The panel consisted of accessibility advocate and design leader Geri Reid , renowned engineer Lauren Beatty , and UX and design researcher Stéphanie Walter , moderated by our product designer, Aprile Elcich . This webinar provided valuable insights for designers, developers, and anyone interested in creating inclusive and accessible digital experiences. Here are the top takeaways from the webinar. Accessibility is best implemented from the start Implementing accessibility in your product can be a daunting task. We asked the panelists what their experience was and what they advise other designers to do. They all agreed that it was essential that you start thinking and applying accessibility very early on in the process. When it's there from the beginning, it's a lot easier to maintain. Accessibility starts with the design system When you want to create an accessible product and encourage your design team to implement accessible design practices, it doesn't work as well when the design system they're following doesn't practice what it preaches. It also gives provides your organization with a rock-solid accessibility foundation to build from. Design systems team can own accessibility We asked the team panel who they thought should own accessibility in an organization. They agreed that accessibility is everyone's responsibility, and because of that, design systems are a great place to have everyone involved. It's crucial to find advocates in your organization and support each other. In the end the design system team will have a decisive say in the design of the product, so they will definitely be involved. Test constantly and follow accessibility guidelines It's not enough to just implement accessibility; you have to make sure it's implemented correctly. Our panelists discussed how to test and what accessibility guidelines to follow. WCAG gives you a great baseline to shoot for. Also there are a host of robust tools that help measure how well you’re meeting those criteria. Automated tests, like end-to-end testing, are effective in scanning for static accessibility violations, while browser extensions — like Wave — and UX dev tools are also available. Newskit also has a web page of testing tools . The four required tests before shipping include: contrast and color testing, interactive elements, keyboard interaction, and zoom level. It's recommended that the technical stuff be removed before testing with disabled people to minimize the cost of usability testing. Proactivity goes a long way No one is born an accessibility expert or advocate. It's important to take initiative and encourage others to do the same. Everyone knows that accessibility is the right thing to do, but it still needs a lot of proactive effort from the people in the organization, whether from a bottom up or top down approach. “Be the change you want to see in your organization." Documenting is a team game The panel learned from experience that documenting and building your design system needs to involve everyone. Designers and engineers need to be comfortable contributing and documenting components, best practices, behaviors and more in your design system. Educate and find the success metric that makes sense to your organization Accessibility is unlikely to be a very straightforward business metric that metric that an organization would care about. It's important that you educate your organization and team on the importance of accessibility. Personal stories and real-world examples can go a long way. It's important to find the right balance and fit for your team to measure and track is essential. Work with the advocates in your team to find how accessibility can link to your KPIs and improve on it. Here are a few useful links provided by the panelists: 4 Required Tests Before Shipping New Features Tools and checkers to help you test against accessibility guidelines Web Accessibility Perspectives Videos A Designer’s Guide to Documenting Accessibility & User Interactions And you can watch the full panel discussion to learn more. You can also find a transcripted recording here .

body_text: HogMail #21: Avoiding the "Product Death Cycle" Andy Vandervell Feb 13, 2023 Contents Welcome to HogMail, our newsletter featuring the best of the PostHog blog, tutorials, product guides, and curated articles on building great products and companies. We send it every two weeks. Signup here so you don't miss it. In HogMail #20 , we looked at a failed startup with product-market fit and 500k active users. So, what comes after product-market fit? More on that soon, but first... Here's what's new on PostHog.com: Raquel Smith on Why 'Product Engineer' is the most fun role I've had in tech Andy Vandervell on Retention vs Churn Rate: Your guide to churn analysis Ian Vanagas on How to use the PostHog API to get insights and persons Abe Basu on Automating user journeys with PostHog and Laudspeaker Words by Andy Vandervell, whose retention is rapidly declining with age. 😢 Avoiding the "Product Death Cycle" If product-market fit isn't enough to succeed, what do you need? In a 2017 article, Brian Balfour says: "The “go-to” answer for almost every question in startups, is “build a great product.” Every time I hear that answer it feels completely unsatisfied. Building a great product is a piece of the puzzle, but it’s far from the full picture." He goes on to argue this mentality can lead to what he calls the Product Death Cycle: In this model, the answer to "how do we grow?" is always launch new feature, but every new launch is slightly less successful than the last, and doesn't lead to lasting growth: Instead, he suggests successful startups ($100M+ in his reckoning) should seek four fits: Market-Product Fit – A variation on product-market fit. Product-Channel Fit – "Products are built to fit with channels. Channels do not mold to products." Channel-Model Fit – Channels are determined by your model, i.e. how you charge and average annual revenue per user. Model-Market Fit – The concept that your market (and # of customers within your market) influence your model." Balfour makes three final points: You need to find four fits to grow to $100M+ company in a venture-backed time frame. Each of these fits influence each other , so you can’t think about them in isolation . The fits are always evolving /changing/breaking. When that happens, you can’t simply change one element, you have to revisit and potentially change them all. body_text: Contenidos ocultar 1 ¿Cómo conseguir préstamos con bajo interés? 2 Mejores opciones de préstamos con bajo interés 2.1 Préstamos con bajo interés en entidades financieras tradicionales 2.2 Préstamos con bajo interés en plataformas digitales 3 ¿Cómo comparar tasas de interés en préstamos? 4 Requisitos para conseguir préstamos con bajo interés 5 ¿Cómo mejorar tu perfil crediticio para obtener préstamos con bajo interés? 6 Préstamos con bajo interés para negocios 7 Préstamos con bajo interés para personas con mal historial crediticio 8 Tipos de préstamos de bajo interés: 8.1 Préstamos con bajo interés para estudiantes 8.2 Préstamos con bajo interés para consolidación de deudas 9 Riesgos de los préstamos con bajo interés 10 Preguntas Frecuentes 11 En Conclusión: ¿Cómo conseguir préstamos con bajo interés? Al momento de considerar si pedir un crédito o no, uno de los factores más importantes a verificar es la tasa de interés. A veces estos costos son sumamente altos y el crédito termina siendo una opción poco conveniente para los solicitantes, sobre todo si la tasa de interés es variable. Sin embargo, existen algunos préstamos con bajo interés a los que podrías optar si quieres tener una suma de dinero pequeña, en poco tiempo y de manera confiable. Los préstamos en línea ahora son la opción de financiamiento más conveniente en Colombia, ya que gran parte de las plataformas prestadoras de este servicio maneja una tasa de interés competitiva e inferior a la de la banca tradicional. Monet es una de estas plataformas. Pero, ¿de qué se tratan los préstamos con bajo interés y cómo solicitarlos? Aquí te contaremos. Mejores opciones de préstamos con bajo interés Si buscas préstamos con bajo interés en Colombia, las entidades bancarias tradicionales ofrecen opciones muy limitadas. Además, la tasa de interés depende del tipo de crédito a solicitar, tu capacidad de endeudamiento y la entidad bancaria. De acuerdo con la Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, a la fecha, la tasa de interés para créditos de consumo y ordinario es de 28,84%; para la modalidad de microcrédito es de 39,20%; y los intereses remuneratorio y moratorio para los créditos de consumo o microcréditos no podrán exceder 1.5 veces del mismo. Préstamos con bajo interés en entidades financieras tradicionales Para saber cuál es la entidad financiera con una tasa de interés más conveniente para ti, ten presente las tasas definidas por la Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. Trata de buscar opciones que estén alejadas de la tasa de usura, ya que este es el monto máximo que debe cobrarse de intereses de crédito. Calcula muy bien cuál sería el monto final del préstamo, incluyendo los intereses y tomando en cuenta si estos son fijos o variables. Préstamos con bajo interés en plataformas digitales Esta podría ser la opción más conveniente para ti si requieres montos pequeños de dinero con baja tasa de interés. En el caso de Monet, no cobramos intereses corrientes sino costos fijos por nuestros servicios. No tenemos costos ocultos y las tarifas por nuestros servicios están disponibles de manera visible en el sitio web https://www.monet.com.co/tarifas-y-costos/ ¿Cómo comparar tasas de interés en préstamos? Para saber la tasa de interés en préstamos puedes utilizar los simuladores de crédito disponibles en línea. La mayoría de las entidades crediticias ponen a disponibilidad de los usuarios una calculadora o simulador de créditos para que sepan cuántas cuotas y plazos escoger para su préstamo. Puedes consultar esta información en las plataformas de tu preferencia, tomar nota de los indicadores más importantes y, finalmente, comparar una opción con otra. Ten en cuenta que la información que ofrecen estas calculadoras es aproximada y eso no significa que el préstamo que vayas a solicitar sea exacto a cómo lo reflejó el simulador. Requisitos para conseguir préstamos con bajo interés Los requisitos para conseguir préstamos con bajo interés varían de acuerdo con la entidad bancaria o plataforma donde lo solicites. Por lo general, debes: Ser mayor de edad Presentar tu cédula de ciudadanía Tener una fuente de ingresos fija comprobable En casos específicos deberás cumplir otros requisitos como: Certificación bancaria o extracto bancario de los últimos 6 meses Monto mínimo de ingresos dependiendo del tipo de crédito Pagaré No estar reportado en centrales de riesgo ¿Cómo mejorar tu perfil crediticio para obtener préstamos con bajo interés? Para mejorar tu perfil crediticio la clave es pagar al día las deudas que tengas y cumplir a cabalidad todos tus compromisos financieros. Por ejemplo, si tienes tarjeta de crédito asegúrate de pagar en el plazo correspondiente la cuota mínima y, si es posible, abona un poco más. Esto te permitirá a corto o mediano plazo aumentar tu cupo de crédito en la tarjeta. Trata de adquirir solo deudas pequeñas que estés plenamente seguro de poder pagar. Para ello debes comparar diferentes opciones de crédito y calcular tu capacidad de endeudamiento. No destines los fondos de los créditos para cubrir gastos hormiga o pagar otras deudas si el tipo de crédito no es para este fin. Si estás reportado en centrales de riesgo igual es posible que adquieras un préstamo en la banca tradicional pero lo más seguro es que por tu perfil de riesgo, los intereses sean mayores. En este caso solicitar un préstamo en línea podría ser tu mejor opción. Los préstamos en línea , en su mayoría, tienen baja tasa de interés y además te ayudarán a mejorar tu perfil crediticio si cumples con el pago en los plazos acordados. Préstamos con bajo interés para negocios Existen créditos y microcréditos para negocios o emprendedores en la banca tradicional que no requieren gran cantidad de papeles o incluso tener experiencia crediticia. Este tipo de créditos tienen requisitos más flexibles con el fin de contribuir con el crecimiento de los pequeños y medianos empresarios. Cada entidad financiera tiene requisitos y tasas diferentes, incluso algunas entidades, como el Banco de Bogotá, manejan cuotas fijas durante la vigencia del préstamo. Algunas compañías de financiamiento también brindan este tipo de créditos y la tasa depende de tu información financiera, por lo que podría ser una opción conveniente de acuerdo con tu capacidad de endeudamiento. Préstamos con bajo interés para personas con mal historial crediticio Para las personas que tienen bajo puntaje crediticio, las mejores opciones de préstamos son las tarjetas de crédito amparadas, créditos de libranza y préstamos en línea. Sin embargo, debes comparar muy bien todas las opciones existentes para reportados, especialmente en la banca tradicional, porque precisamente por ser ciudadanos con riesgo mayor para el sistema, podrían asignarles tasas mayores. Tipos de préstamos de bajo interés: Algunos tipos de préstamos de bajo interés son los anticipos de nómina, tarjetas de crédito amparadas, créditos de libre inversión, préstamos en línea y microcréditos. Este tipo de créditos es más conveniente si las cuotas o tasas son fijas y no variables. Hay otros tipos de préstamos de bajo interés que son para estudiantes y para consolidación de deudas. Préstamos con bajo interés para estudiantes Con el propósito de contribuir con la inclusión financiera de Colombia, algunas entidades financieras ofrecen préstamos con bajo interés para estudiantes. Los fondos de estos créditos se destinan al pago de estudios de pregrado, posgrado o estudios técnicos de los solicitantes, aún cuando no tengan historial crediticio. Según Rankia, las principales opciones de créditos educativos son de las entidades Bancolombia, Serfinanza, BBVA, Banco Pichincha, Banco Davivienda, Banco de Bogotá y el Banco AV Villas. Además, otra de las opciones disponibles para el financiamiento de estudios es el ICETEX, donde los plazos, importes y tasas son variables. Préstamos con bajo interés para consolidación de deudas Este tipo de crédito es el más recomendable para cumplir con el pago de tus deudas. Este pago se hace a través de la consolidación de tarjetas de crédito para cancelar deudas. Por ejemplo, en lugar de pagar una cuota diferente por cada tarjeta de crédito, puedes unificar todas las deudas para que tengas un pago, plazo y tasa de interés únicos. De esta forma, la tasa de interés podría bajar considerablemente, aunque no es algo seguro para todos los casos. Riesgos de los préstamos con bajo interés Aunque los préstamos con bajo interés pueden parecer muy atractivos, es importante conocer los riesgos asociados: Tasas variables: Algunas tasas de interés son variables, lo que significa que pueden aumentar con el tiempo. Si la tasa de interés aumenta significativamente, tus pagos mensuales también aumentarán. Costos ocultos: Además de la tasa de interés, los préstamos pueden tener otros costos asociados, como comisiones por apertura, por cancelación anticipada o por mora. Es importante leer detenidamente el contrato antes de firmarlo para conocer todos los costos. Endeudamiento excesivo: Pedir un préstamo puede ser tentador, pero es importante evaluar tu capacidad de pago antes de solicitar uno. Endeudarse en exceso puede generar estrés financiero y afectar tu capacidad para cumplir con otras obligaciones. Preguntas Frecuentes ¿Puedo adquirir un préstamo con bajo interés aunque esté reportado en centrales de riesgo? Sí, pero debes hacer un estudio exhaustivo de las opciones disponibles, ya que algunas de ellas incluso establecen tasas de interés mayores debido a tu perfil de riesgo. ¿Es posible que se me otorgue un crédito si soy estudiante? Sí, existen préstamos específicos para cubrir tus gastos estudiantiles. ¿Puedo pedir un crédito para mi negocio aunque no tenga experiencia crediticia? Sí, existen opciones de créditos y microcréditos especialmente dirigidas a empresarios y emprendedores. ¿Cómo saber cuál es la opción de crédito más conveniente para mí? Debes comparar diferentes opciones. Los simuladores y comparadores de crédito pueden ser muy útiles para esto. Sin embargo, te recomendamos que siempre busques asesoría de un experto en finanzas si aún tienes dudas sobre qué decisión tomar. En Conclusión: Los préstamos con bajo interés podrían ser de gran ayuda para tu salud financiera, especialmente si tienes poco puntaje o historial crediticio y tu capacidad de endeudamiento es moderada. Compara siempre las mejores opciones para tu situación específica y plantéate metas financieras y cifras realistas para aprovechar al máximo estos préstamos. Para empezar con una opción conservadora que mida tu capacidad de endeudamiento y te permita cumplir gastos y responsabilidades financieras con bajo interés, puedes probar plataformas de préstamos en línea como Monet. title: Keeping Up with Changes in International Messaging
summary: 2022 was a year of massive regulatory change in the telecom industry around the world. Here are some specifics.
body_text: The last several months have seen massive regulatory change in the telecom industry around the world. Here are some of the highlights. New sending rules in Singapore and Saudi Arabia Sender ID is the name or number that is displayed as the sender of the SMS message to the receiver of the SMS message. Countries have different practices around sender ID use . In 2022 Iran, Singapore, and Morocco all began requiring preregistration for sender IDs . Singapore launched a full SMS Sender ID Registry (SSIR) Regime under which only local business entities or foreign entities with a local physical presence can communicate via text messages. As part of their efforts to reduce text messaging spam, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) now requires that international businesses that send SMS into the country do so via an aggregator that has a direct connection with appointed SMS hub providers. To comply with the requirements, providers like Plivo need to have a No Objection Certificate (NOC) on file for customers’ messaging traffic. A NOC is similar to a Letter of Authorization (LOA) used in other countries. KSA began enforcing the requirement on February 1. Plivo customers can download a NOC template [DOC], complete it, scan it, and return it via support ticket . New content regulations in the UK, Iran, and Vietnam The UK now requires that the content of URLs sent in SMS messages toward the UK be preapproved by a service provider. Businesses must share with their provider their company name and website address, their sender ID, and the contents of the messages they plan to send. Iran now scrubs messages at an operator level for all messages that contain URLs. Vietnam now requires content whitelisting at an operator level. New short code requirements in NZ and BR Meanwhile, regulators in New Zealand and Brazil are now encouraging messages to be sent via short codes; messages sent via other number types will experience poor deliverability. Plivo now offers short codes in both New Zealand and Brazil for a better messaging experience. A single theme: combat fraud All of these changes indicate that countries are tightening regulations to combat fraud. Telecom regulators in more countries are beginning to require pre registration and content whitelisting. At the same time, processes around the globe are becoming more streamlined to ensure faster and safer communications. Someday we may live in a world in which, when you receive a message from a Nigerian prince, it really is from African royalty.

title: How we improved reporting and monitoring of test automation results
summary: Over the last few years, we completely refactored what was described in our previous article about how we use the ELK sta...
body_text: Over the last few years, we completely refactored what was described in our previous article about how we use the ELK stack for an overview of our test automation results , but some core concepts remain valid and applicable. As we have moved to a Continuous Delivery approach with our new web application with dozens of daily releases of our main product, it has become more crucial to identify the causes of end-to-end test failures. Every day we fight against test flakiness , i.e. failures unrelated to actual defects in the application under test, and have achieved an average success rate of more than 99% on our Selenium-based tests. This means less than 1% of failed tests on stable main branch in the overnight runs, indicating that there are still inevitable occasional failures that might cause uncertainty. It’s a well known problem of UI automation that can happen frequently, especially on a staging environment where we are not mocking any backend service. In our view, the best answer is to empower every QA engineer or developer to be able to easily and quickly identify if a specific test failure is only related to the branch/PR where it was detected. Good reporting tools and dashboards that allow one to gather an overview of test executions across all repository workflows are therefore essential. Current setup Our updated setup for end-to-end test execution, reporting, and monitoring includes: GitHub Actions (GHA) workflows Custom runners on Google Cloud (GCP) for test jobs Cluecumber Maven plugin for test reports generation Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket for test reports storage A test framework plugin that produces Kafka log entries from Cucumber JSON report files Kafka message broker Logstash for processing Kafka messages Elasticsearch for data storage Kibana for data visualization and exploration Grafana and Slack for alerting on recurring test failures Test reports storage in the cloud We previously used in-house Jenkins instances for test executions and the reports generated by the Cluecumber plugin (html pages) could be attached to each job run as artifacts and Jenkins would also serve them as web pages when accessed in a browser. With test execution now triggered through GitHub Actions, and test jobs executed within custom runners on GCP, we needed to find a solution for storing and accessing the test reports. Attaching them as zipped artifacts to each GHA workflow run was the first solution, but it was inconvenient as it required downloading and unzipping each report, also making any direct linking from dashboards more complicated. We thought about using something already available in the trivago tech stack and specifically opted for leveraging Google Cloud storage by uploading the test reports to a GCS bucket, serving them as web pages through a gcs-proxy application supporting file listing that is inspired by https://GitHub.com/springernature/gcs-proxy . That’s how we created a “test report server” to suit our needs. After the tests execution is completed, the current test flow involves: Logging tests results (from Cucumber JSON files) to Kafka Generating a test report as a html page with attachments using the Cluecumber plugin Uploading the generated test report folder to the “test report server” GCS bucket Sharing the link to the test report as a GitHub status badge, comment on a PR, message to Slack etc., based on the workflow requirements. The upload step is simple and requires running a gsutil command within the GitHub Actions jobs: name : Upload test report to the GCS Bucket id : uploadTestReport if : ${{ always() }} run : | gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account serviceaccount-email@our-test-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com gsutil -m rsync -r "${{ env.REPORT_LOCAL_PATH }}" "${{ env.DESTINATION_BUCKET }}/${{ GitHub.repository }}/${{ GitHub.workflow }}/${{ GitHub.run_id }}" We decided to organize the reports by repository, workflow, and run id. This proved very efficient, allowing for easy scale up when more teams within the company started using our test report server for their projects, storing end-to-end and API automated tests reports as well as Webpack bundle analyzer reports. Kibana and Grafana As logging to Kafka includes the test reports links, we can’t only look at a failure message already within our Kibana dashboards, but also easily reach a complete test report with just one click, immediately accessing steps execution details, screenshots, and video recordings. A set of different panels and filters allows each of our QA engineers and developers to quickly focus on a certain branch or test result. We currently have a main template for dashboards, reused for different projects and test workflows, but the availability of multiple fields with detailed data also enables each individual team to build their own dashboards with relevant information and filtering. A further recent addition to the existing setup has been to leverage Grafana to trigger notifications to a Slack channel when a single test scenario fails across multiple branches/PRs. This way we can avoid actively scanning for flaky tests during the day and it’s a support to flakiness detection jobs that we run overnight on the application main branch. The Grafana queries look like: doctype: "regression_tests_warp" AND (project: "warp_core_mobile" OR project: "warp_core_desktop") AND status: FAILED We perform aggregation by scenario name, and apply a given threshold on the unique count of base URLs to determine the number of different preview machines on which the failures are occurring. Since the base URL is tied to the PR/branch name, it provides an easy way to identify whether the failure is specific to a particular branch or widespread. In case the query condition is met, an alert notification is sent as a Slack message, containing indications about the failing test(s) and quick links to the more detailed Kibana dashboard. Conclusion As we iterated over our original approach to test results reporting and monitoring that keeps relying on Kafka and the ELK stack, we managed to drastically increase trust in test automation by providing extensive feedback within quick reach, also adding Grafana alerting capabilities to the mix. At the same time, the cloud test reports storage project proved to be a valuable resource for other teams that adopted it, as it is not tied to specific test types, test frameworks, or reporting tools used. For additional details about the Cluecumber reporting plugin you can check a previous article on our blog .
